name: What are the most common hidden costs in a home extension?

mainEntity.name: What are the most common hidden costs in a home extension?
mainEntity.text: What are the most common hidden costs in a home extension?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden costs are one of the biggest reasons home extension budgets run over. Structural reinforcement is common, especially when the project opens walls, adds a second story, or changes the roofline. Electrical and plumbing upgrades can add significant cost if the current systems are undersized or outdated. HVAC modifications are also easy to overlook because the new space often needs separate ducting or equipment adjustments. Other costs include permits, engineering, energy compliance, window and door upgrades, matching existing finishes, and repairs uncovered during demolition. Site access can add labor if materials need to be carried through a tight side yard or if staging space is limited. Homeowners should ask for a detailed scope that identifies exclusions and allowances so they can compare bids fairly. A realistic contingency fund is essential because older homes in particular often reveal surprises once construction begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common hidden costs include structural reinforcement, upgraded electrical or plumbing, HVAC changes, window and door upgrades, insulation, permitting, engineering, and finish mismatches with the existing home. Demolition and site access problems can also increase the budget.
